# Goal
kama round 95 (L1 KamaR95, the only committer and integration owner). Lane repo /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin — local model serving and
endpoint health (llama.cpp router mode, served-model identity, probe verdicts). Three frozen claims are declared in
/home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin/plans/round-95-claims.md — READ IT FULL FIRST. Its predicates, counters, controls, kill rules and disclosed limits are frozen and bind
you. This wave ATTACKS work that is already landed; it never changes a frozen predicate and never edits a tracked
lane file.

- C1 operability: `tools/kama-probe.sh`'s `ROUTER_PY` no longer decides a candidate's file state on a wall clock.
  Work is bounded by `MAX_STEPS` (4 000 000 read/seek steps) and `MAX_META` (512 MiB header position); the pass-level
  limit is `20 + 15 * ncand` seconds in `router_file_states`. Frozen counter `tools/round95-router-budget.py`
  (10 cells, two passes: natural then synthetic CPU load). Your job is to find where the verdict is STILL not a
  function of the bytes, or where removing the clock lost a protection the clock was providing.
- C2 depth: `SKILL.md` section `## Listen port and slot-count setters (round 95 revision)` — 106 population rows
  (P01-P106) and 9 per-entry-point decision rows (`R20` port, `R21` n_parallel) over the pinned llama.cpp b12177
  archive (sha256 f50a52f4ba45dd5b4b906db97cf230ce2e3b1117a0b9017411322ecba63eea13). Frozen counter
  `tools/round95-setter-sweep.py`. Its predicate grades population/rows/bound/source/derived cells and the decision
  id sets; the PROSE TRUTH of a row is not graded by it — that read is yours.
- C3 calibration: `tools/round95-freeze-audit.py` grades the plan itself (every receipt path it names exists at the
  rev; every `token=` on a predicate line appears in that counter's bytes; every cited S-id resolves).

Revisions: base B=2011161d5e5612fa953708cf54084b7f10ce99b1. The freeze commit, M1 (probe change) and M2 (SKILL
section + sources + lesson) are named in the round report; ask the L1 if you need a hash that is not yet in
`git -C /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin log --oneline -8`.
Pinned sources: single files at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/b12177/<path>; archive at
https://codeload.github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tar.gz/refs/tags/b12177 (verify the sha256 above before using it).
Host: 32-core multi-agent box, load frequently 50-200+; every timing cell carries its `load1` and uses within-run
ratios.

# Contract (binding on every seat)
- Read-only in the lane repo except your own out dir /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin/.ufo/waves/round-95/w1/out/<YOUR-NAME>/ (mkdir -p) and your `Report:`
  trailer file. Never edit a tracked lane file (tools/, tests/, corpus/, SKILL.md, SCORECARD.md, LOG.md, plans/,
  registry/). Candidate files go into your out dir; the L1 integrates.
- Every `Report:` trailer path is relative to /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin — write it at /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin/<that path>, and nowhere else.
- Scratch: /fast/scratch/hyaku/kama-r95/<YOUR-NAME>/ only — your OWN seat name, never another seat's (round-91 R3:
  twin seats sharing a scratch path wiped each other's files). mkdir -p, export TMPDIR to it, pass it as --work to
  any counter. At most one clone: `git clone --shared /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin <scratch>/wt` then `git -C <scratch>/wt checkout
  --detach <rev>`. NEVER `git worktree add` from the lane. Any fixture repo: D=$(mktemp -d -p <scratch>) &&
  git -C "$D" init -q, and verify `git -C "$D" rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals $D before any git write; never pass
  an empty or unchecked variable to `git -C`; never commit with a throwaway identity anywhere else. Remove your
  scratch dir before you yield (`rm -rf -- <scratch>`) after copying receipts into your out dir. A seat that ends
  with its tree still on disk reports that as a defect of its own.
- Never commit, push, fetch, stash, add, reset, pull, or run any mutating git or jj command in the lane or the fleet
  repo (read-only git and `jj --ignore-working-copy` are fine). Never touch the fleet root
  /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin (MANIFEST.json, templates/, scripts/, .ufo/state, .scratch/), sibling lanes
  (read-only for the connector), /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokuknow, or /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/kama-shokunin/considerthese/.
- Live endpoints: NEVER send a POST, load, unload or completion to 127.0.0.1:1234 (the operator's live llama.cpp
  router). GET /v1/models and GET /props on 1234 only where your item says so. Everything else runs on stubs or
  lane-owned children you start on free loopback ports and kill (process group) before you yield. Never mutate host
  sysctls or services; never kill a process you did not start. `sysctl user.max_user_namespaces` MUST NOT be written
  by any seat (host incident 2026-11-05).
- CPU burners: if you raise load deliberately, you MUST kill every one of them in a `finally`, verified by pgrep
  returning nothing for your own pattern, before you yield. A leaked burner blocks every lane's wave (host incident
  2026-11-08, three reaps in one night).
- Network: read-only GET on public URLs your item names. No credentials.
- Leaf: never delegate. Never pass or choose a model. Never message agent://all.
- Tooling authorization (operator, 2026-10-19): you may install or upgrade tools that help your task. Read
  /home/vgpnk/.omp/agent/RULES.md first (official channels, update-safety gate); record tool, version, channel and
  reason in your report. Pacman guard: ALL pacman transactions are PAUSED host-wide — never run pacman
  -S/-Sy/-Syu/-U/-R, never restart a host service; use uv tool, npx, or an official release binary in ~/.local/bin.
- Run only the checks your item names plus what you need to falsify it. An unrun check has not passed. Report exact
  commands, true exit codes, and the full hash of every revision you measured. Do not soften findings: a reproduced
  false green, a behaviour change against base, or a misstated row is the most valuable output.
- Final report (your Report: file): sections Scope, Commands and outputs (with exit codes), Findings (each with an
  evidence pointer: path:line or command output; label each finding BLOCKER / DEFECT / NOTE), Deliverables (paths in
  your out dir), and a last line exactly `VERDICT: <holds|falsified|partial> — <one line>`. Under 120 lines.
